BILL NO. 10,189, 2018
(From Mr. Marcelo Ortiz)
Declares the sweet known as "TAIADA" as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Brazil and the city of Caçapava.

DISPACH:
TO THE COMMITTEES OF:
CULTURE; AND
CONSTITUTION AND JUSTICE AND CITIZENSHIP (ART. 54 RICD).

CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Conclusive Consideration by the Committees - Art. 24 II
The National Congress decrees:

Art. 1. Provides for the recognition of the cultural importance of the sweet known as
“TAIADA”, nationally known and typical of the state of São Paulo, originating from the city of Caçapava, for
the Brazilian tourist circuit.

Art. 2º O The sweet known as “TAIADA” is hereby constituted as Intangible Cultural Heritage
of Brazil for all legal purposes.

Art. 3. This law shall enter into force on the date of its publication.

JUSTIFICATION

"Taiada is a typical sweet from the Brazilian city of Caçapava, in the state of São Paulo, made from
garapa (sugar cane juice), with cassava flour and ginger, resulting in a crumbly texture and enhancing the
spicy flavor.

The production of taiada is artisanal and a family tradition passed down from father to son, mainly
in the rural areas of this municipality. As the sweet is made with ingredients of high nutritional and caloric
value and is easily transportable, it was taken by rural workers to the fields and by soldiers in the army on
marching to be used as an energy source during work and effort, and also to sweeten drinks like coffee with
milk.

The name "taiada" is a corruption of "talhada", the participle of the verb "talhar", which
gently acquired a Caipira accent, becoming popularly known as "taiada".

After the manual cutting of sugar cane, where the best ones are selected, they are transported to
the mill where they are ground. The resulting cassava juice is then poured into a copper pot, boiled for
approximately 90 minutes, until it reaches the desired consistency (a little in cold water and it seems like
candy that can be stretched); taken off the heat and mixed with cassava flour and ground ginger; the mixture
is then poured into a traditional wooden mold in the shape of a square, suitable for this purpose, and left
in the mold for an hour when it hardens, cools and takes its shape, after which it can be removed from the
molds. In the book "Miçangas Folclóricas", by folklorist Francisco Pereira da Silva, known
May 2018
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES
Tuesday 15 119

As Chico Triste, there is a recipe dictated by Benedito Martins.
Those born in Caçapava, or living in the municipality, are affectionately called "taiadas," in reference to the sweet found in that city, with several versions for the origin of this nickname, but almost all are related to young men who served mandatory military service at the Brazilian Army barracks and, upon leaving, would stop at a bar and, among other things, buy the sweet, and those from other cities would bid farewell to the Caçapavenses by calling them "taiada," and despite the sweet no longer being as popular as it once was, the nickname is still widely used.

This justification, extracted from the free encyclopedia, Wikipedia, https://pt.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taiada, clearly demonstrates the importance of the sweet to our country's popular culture, which is why I present this bill in line with the excellent work of rescuing popular culture formulated by the Municipal Secretary of Culture, Sports, and Leisure of Caçapava, Professor Fabrício Correia, in accordance with the cultural formulations of Mayor Fernando Cid Diniz Borges.

Therefore, we request the support of the Honorable Members of this House for the approval of the present bill.

This Law amends Article 41-A of Law No. 9,096, of September 19, 1995, to modify the criteria for distributing the Party Fund, providing for the reservation of 10% (ten percent) of the Fund for equal distribution among parties that comply with legal rules regarding the promotion of the political participation of the Black community.

**JUSTIFICATION**

It is common knowledge that the recent political reform approved by the National Congress established the Electoral Fund for campaign financing. Despite the creation of this new fund, the rules of the Party Fund remain unchanged. It is worth noting that funds from the Party Fund can also be used for electoral campaigns, although its primary purpose has historically been to cover party expenses. This model has not been significantly altered since the creation of the Fund.

The main objective of this proposal is to modify the distribution and application of Party Fund resources to introduce a system of rewarding parties that meet specific requirements, always aimed at encouraging political participation from "minorized" sectors of our society.

This bill proposes to encourage the participation of the Black community in politics. It is undeniable that there is reluctance in political and party life regarding Black participation, which contrasts with our population's ethnic composition. It is true that Blacks are currently under-represented.

In this context, we believe it is important to change the way resources from the Party Fund are distributed to establish incentive policies for parties aimed at improving our democracy. In other words: a party that meets certain conditions will be rewarded with additional portions of the Party Fund.

As mentioned, our goal is to initiate this new model by establishing requirements related to the political participation of the Black community. Specifically, we propose to reserve 10% (ten percent) of Party Fund resources to be distributed among organizations that:

BILL NO. 10,206, OF 2018
(From Mr. Dr. Sinval Malheiros)
Elevates the Egg Festival of Bastos/SP to the status of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Brazil.

DISPOSITION:
TO THE COMMITTEES OF:
CULTURE; AND
CONSTITUTION AND JUSTICE AND CITIZENSHIP (ART. 54 RICD).
CONSIDERATION:
Proposal Subject to Conclusive Consideration by the Committees - Art. 24 II
THE NATIONAL CONGRESS decrees:

Art. 1. This Law aims to recognize the importance of the Egg Festival of Bastos/SP as the main event promoting the significance and trade of eggs in Brazil.

Art. 2. The Egg Festival of Bastos/SP is established as intangible cultural heritage of Brazil, for all legal purposes.

Art. 3. This Law enters into force on the date of its publication.

JUSTIFICATION
Bastos is a Brazilian municipality, located in the interior of the state of São Paulo, with a population of approximately twenty thousand inhabitants. It is known, especially, for its egg production, being known as “the national capital of eggs”. And as one of the reasons that underpin its importance in domestic egg production, there is the Egg Festival of Bastos.

The city, founded by Japanese immigrants, began to invest in egg production after World War II as a way to revive the local economy. Thanks to tireless and excellent work, the activity strengthened and the city consolidated as a reference pole in the area, with more than seven decades dedicated to the practice, considered the main exponent of the segment since the 1960s.

The municipality has over 33 million birds intended for egg production, and according to the local Rural Syndicate president in 2017, Mr. Katsuhide Maki, the farms of the municipality produce 216 units per second, with 18.7 million eggs per day. Annually, Bastos produces around 10 billion eggs, which represents approximately 25% of Brazil's annual production of 40 billion.

Bastos, therefore, producing alone 25% of a food of immense nutritional value and fundamental importance to the Brazilian, being a rich protein and vitamin source at a price generally more accessible than red meat, for example.

Given such a redemption brought about by egg production, Bastos began to hold its Egg Festival. The event was born in 1948 and gained importance over time. Before
May 2018
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES
Tuesday 15 125

Held every five years, the festival has become annual and today approaches its 59th edition, highlighting the
importance of the location and its dedication to egg production.
It is an event of extreme importance and attractiveness for the surrounding regions, attracting the
interest of numerous producers in the sector. In 2017, for example, eighty-two companies were exhibitors at
the event, demonstrating its magnitude and its growing importance. From 2016 to 2017, there was a 30%
increase in the number of exhibitors.
The event offers a little bit of everything: recreational activities related to eggs (contests to see who eats
the most), competitions aimed at assessing the quality of eggs and concluding with the best one, workshops
and lectures intended to disseminate information about the food, its production and techniques, and even
serving as a pole for technological discussions on the topic.
Undeniably, the festival functions as a true driving force for egg production in Brazil, with characteristics
of cultural, informational, educational, and commercial diffusion, demonstrating that it is a cultural and
intangible heritage. The tradition and quality of what is produced there are of fundamental importance not
only for Bastos, or even for the large state of São Paulo, but for Brazil, as it is the largest exponent of
production of one of the main national foods.
For all these reasons, we believe that the Egg Festival of Bastos/SP requires formal recognition by this
National Congress and, subsequently, by the Executive Power, by sanctioning its existence as a cultural and
intangible heritage of our nation.
Brazil needs to learn to value its significant traditions more, which transmit good customs, and perfect
them, something that Bastos has been an example of. This is because it has transformed this recreational
event into a commercial opportunity and a means of disseminating knowledge and technologies, without
losing the joy and leisure provided by the festival.
Thus, we submit this proposal to the consideration of the esteemed colleagues and urge them to approve
it. Because taking care of cities (and their traditions) is taking care of people.
Chamber of Sessions, May 9, 2018.

Doctor and Federal Deputy (PODEMOS/SP)

**Justification**

The participation of state-owned companies in economic activity should be guided by significant collective interest or national security imperatives, in order to achieve goals such as ensuring national development and reducing social and regional inequalities, among others, as established by our Federal Constitution.

Indirect public administration, which includes state-owned companies, must adhere to constitutional principles of legality, impersonality, morality, publicity, and efficiency. The general need to bid is essential in this regard, even for public companies and mixed economy societies.

According to Article 173, §1, of the Federal Constitution, the law will establish the legal statute for public companies, mixed economy societies, and their subsidiaries that engage in economic activity related to the production or commercialization of goods or the provision of services, including provisions on bidding and contracting for works, services, purchases, and alienations.

Law No. 13.303 of June 30, 2016, known as the Legal Statute of State-Owned Companies, regulated Article 173, §1, and established the legal statute for public companies, mixed economy societies, and their subsidiaries within the scope of the Union, states, Federal District, and municipalities.

Section 5 of Article 1 of Law No. 13.303/2016 is clear in defining that for the public company and the mixed economy society that participate in a consortium in the condition of operator are subject to the bidding rules provided in the Legal Statute of State-Owned Enterprises, as it reads:

§ 5. Public companies and mixed economy societies that participate in a consortium, as provided in Article 279 of Law No. 6,404 of December 15, 1976, shall be subject to the regime established in this Law, in the condition of operator.

In accordance with Article 28 of Law No. 13.303/2016, contracts with third parties for the provision of services to public companies and mixed economy societies, including engineering and advertising, the acquisition and rental of goods, and the alienation of goods and assets forming part of their respective patrimony, must be preceded by a tender process.

Therefore, the procurement of goods and services by consortia operated by Petrobras and the assignment by the state-owned company of rights for the exploration, development, and production of oil and natural gas should be preceded by a tender process, and the bidding process must comply with the requirements established by Law No. 13.303/2016.

Article 1 of Decree No. 9.355 of April 25, 2018, establishes a special procedure for the assignment of rights for the exploration, development, and production of oil and natural gas by Petrobras, as provided for in Article 29, Article 61, paragraph (1), and Article 63 of Law No. 9.478 of August 6, 1997, and in Article 31 of Law No. 12.351 of December 22, 2010.

It is important to note that: Article 29 of Law No. 9.478/1997 only allows for the transfer of the concession contract; Article 61, paragraph (1), essentially aims to prevent favoritism to Petrobras in the acquisition of rights related to petroleum activities; and Article 63 only authorizes Petrobras to form consortia. Article 31 of Law No. 12.351/2010 is generic and applicable to all companies, except for the sole paragraph, which does not allow Petrobras to assign rights related to its minimum participation.

Furthermore, all these legal provisions predate the promulgation of Law No. 13.302/2016.

Thus, Decree No. 9.355/2018 exceeds regulatory power and the limits of legislative delegation by establishing a special procedure for the assignment of rights for the exploration, development, and production of oil, natural gas, and other fluid hydrocarbons by Petrobras.

"Strictly across the country, public transportation fares undergo adjustments based, typically, on inflation indices. Therefore, CBTU claims mere inflation loss compensation.

However, in the specific case of Recife, to give an example, the fare correction will be significantly higher than the accumulated inflation during the period since the last adjustment. This adjustment occurred in February 2012, when the fare was set at R$ 1.60. With monetary updating based on IGP-M (FGV), this value would today be R$ 2.27, well below the proposed R$ 3.00 increase. CBTU adjusted the fare by an incredible 24.3% above mere monetary correction.

In addition to the inconsistency of the justification that claims monetary correction while there was an adjustment above accumulated inflation, the increase is abusive and sudden, generating a high degree of uncertainty and economic-financial instability for public service users.

Access to public transportation is a social right guaranteed in the Federal Constitution (Article 6). The purpose of this proposal is to protect the fundamental rights of the population, preventing setbacks in sensitive issues regarding the basic rights of the Brazilian citizen.

Article 49, Clause V, of the Federal Constitution (CF) attributes an extremely important exclusive competence to the National Congress, namely, the power to invalidate executive normative acts that exceed the regulatory power. Furthermore, Clauses X and XI confer to this body the competences of "inspecting and controlling, directly or through any of its chambers, the acts of the executive power, including those of indirect administration" and of "ensuring the preservation of its legislative competence in the face of the normative attribution of the other powers."

Therefore, it can be observed that the aforementioned increase, authorized through the CBTU Board of Directors (CONAD), far exceeded the regulatory power granted to the executive power, being absolutely incompatible with the guiding principles of the 1988 Federal Constitution.

Thus, considering that this fare increase represents a clear disrespect for the constitutional order - characterizing, therefore, a flagrant "excession of regulatory power or of the limits of legislative delegation," as per Article 49, Clause V of the Magna Carta - it is incumbent upon the National Congress, hearing the just concerns of the population, to, through this legislative decree, guarantee access to public transportation by invalidating Item 09 of the minutes of the 364th (three hundred sixty-fourth) Regular Meeting of the Board of Directors of the Brazilian Company of Urban Trains - CBTU, held on February 26, 2018, which approves the fare increase for metro in various Brazilian capitals.

## RESOLUTION DRAFT

**NO. 314, 2018**
**(From Mr. Rodrigo Garcia and others)**

Designates a space in the Chamber of Deputies as "Deputado Joaquim Nabuco" and provides for other measures.

**DISPOSAL:**

To the Presidency of the Chamber of Deputies

**CONSIDERATION:**

Proposition subject to plenary consideration

The Chamber of Deputies Presidency resolves:

**Article 1:** The space in the Chamber of Deputies' Noble Hall shall be designated "Deputado Joaquim Nabuco" and will house a bronze bust of the personality and a corresponding plaque.

**Article 2:** The House's technical bodies, after study, shall indicate an appropriate location within the Noble Hall for the designation of the space and the placement of the bust.

**Article 3:** The Chamber of Deputies Presidency shall arrange for the fabrication of a plaque with the appropriate inscriptions for the tribute and shall set a date for its unveiling.

**Article 4:** This Resolution shall enter into force on the date of its publication.

**JUSTIFICATION**

This draft aims to honor the extraordinary figure of Joaquim Nabuco (J. Aurélio Barreto N. de Araújo), known and admired as an intellectual, writer, sociologist, jurist, diplomat, and, most importantly, as one of the icons of the abolitionist movement in Brazil, by placing his bust in a suitable location.

Joaquim Nabuco was born in Recife on August 19, 1849, the son of Senator Nabuco de Araújo and his wife Ana Benigna de Sá Barreto. He passed away in Washington, USA, on January 17, 1910.

He grew up within influential families of Pernambuco's politics. His father, "the Nabuco de Araújo" family - father and grandfather - were senators of the Empire; his mother's side was "the Paes Barreto" family.

He entered the diplomatic service and served in London and Washington from 1876 to 1879. He was later drawn to politics, captivated by the abolitionist cause, which he dedicated himself to throughout his life.

From 1879 to 1889, he served as a Federal Deputy for the state of Pernambuco, elected by the Liberal Party, where he stood out as the main parliamentary leader in the abolitionist struggle.

Ahead of his time, Joaquim Nabuco not only advocated for the end of slavery; he also fought for the basic rights of newly freed slaves, such as education and fair employment. He also fiercely advocated for land reform and the establishment of a secular state.

Upon the proclamation of the Republic in 1889, he staunchly defended the monarchy and withdrew from public life to dedicate himself to study and his literary works.

During this period, he practiced law and journalism; he cultivated relationships with prominent figures of Brazilian literature, such as Machado de Assis, José Veríssimo, and Lúcio de Mendonça. It is believed that the creation of the Brazilian Academy of Letters in 1897 was due to the gatherings of these privileged minds.
May 2018
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES
Tuesday 15 137

Your intellectual collection includes essays, articles, books, and speeches; the work is intricate and
widely consulted in the present day.
Among his works, we would highlight “Abolitionism (1883)”, which depicts the social evolution of Brazil and
the racial question; and “My Formation (1900)”, a biographical creation in which his famous phrase is recited:
"Slavery will remain for a long time as the national characteristic of Brazil."
In 1889, after numerous appeals, Nabuco returns to public life and accepts an invitation from the government
to defend Brazil in the issue involving the borders with then English Guiana. In 1905, he becomes the first
ambassador of Brazil in the United States.
His history and his legacy of ideas have been repeatedly recognized and honored. In
2010, for example, in partnership with the Brazilian Academy of Letters (ABL) and with the support of the
Joaquim Nabuco Foundations (Fundaj) and Armando Álvares Penteado (Faap), the Chamber of Deputies
paid a well-deserved tribute to Joaquim Nabuco on the centenary of his death. On that occasion, the focus of
the celebrations highlighted his life as a parliamentarian.
The year 2018 marks 140 years since Joaquim Nabuco's election to the Chamber of Deputies. It is only right
that the Chamber honors this great figure of our history once again, this time by placing a bust already
existing in this House in a prominent space within the Noble Hall.
It is with this objective that I submit to the noble peers this Resolution Project, for which I request special
support in its approval, in memory of Joaquim Nabuco's history, his contribution to social causes in the
country, and his brilliant performance as a parliamentarian in this House.

**Article 5** The Chamber of Deputies' Desk shall issue the necessary instructions for the conferment of the Maria da Penha Medal within thirty days of the publication of this Resolution.

**Article 6** This Resolution shall enter into force on the date of its publication.

**Justification**

The proposal for the Maria da Penha Medal, to be conferred by the Chamber of Deputies, aims to honor individuals, institutions, and social movements, both national and international, that, with the same spirit of struggle as Maria da Penha, have distinguished themselves through significant initiatives in the fight against violence against women.

Above all, it is a recognition of the historical role played by the Brazilian woman Maria da Penha in the struggle for women's rights. In 1983, Maria da Penha was victimized by her then-husband with a gunshot wound to the back while she was sleeping, and as a result of this assault, she became paraplegic. After other violences by her ex-husband, Maria da Penha initiated a long and exhausting legal process that took 19 years and 6 months until her ex-husband's conviction in 2002 to eight years in prison.

More than the conviction of her aggressor, Maria da Penha's struggle led the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights of the Organization of American States (OAS) to condemn Brazil in 2001 for negligence, omission, and tolerance regarding domestic violence against women, and to recommend the adoption of public policies aimed at preventing, punishing, and eradicating violence against women. As a direct consequence of this condemnation, the National Congress made new efforts to approve legislation aimed at preventing and punishing domestic violence in Brazil.

After years of debates, the National Congress enacted and the President of the Republic sanctioned Law 11.340 of August 7, 2006, deservedly known as the "Maria da Penha Law," which establishes mechanisms to curb domestic and family violence against women, in accordance with Article 226, § 8 of the Federal Constitution, the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, and the Inter-American Convention to Prevent, Punish and Eradicate Violence against Women; provides for the creation of Domestic and Family Violence against Women Courts; amends the Criminal Procedure Code, the Penal Code, and the Penal Execution Code; and establishes other provisions.

Despite the landmark represented by the Maria da Penha Law, the sad reality is that the story of domestic violence suffered by Maria da Penha still repeats itself daily in thousands of Brazilian homes. Some data from the Maria da Penha Institute highlight this dramatic scenario: (i) every 2 seconds a woman is a victim of physical or verbal violence in Brazil; (ii) every 2.6 seconds a woman is a victim of verbal abuse; (iii) every 6.3 seconds a woman is a victim of a threat of violence; (iv) every 2 minutes a woman is a victim of a firearm; (v) every 22.5 seconds a woman is a victim of

every 4.6 seconds a woman is a victim of harassment at work; (viii) every 6.1 seconds a woman is
a victim of physical harassment in public transportation.
In turn, the 11th edition of the Brazilian Public Security Annual, released in 2017,
records 49,497 cases of rape and 4,657 homicides of women in 2016. From another perspective, the
research "Visible and Invisible: The Victimization of Women in Brazil", conducted by Datafolha in 2016,
found that: (i) for 73% of the Brazilian population, violence against women has increased in the last 10
years; (ii) 66% of the population have witnessed a woman being a victim of some form of violence; (iii)

In the context of persistent violence against women, we believe it is the duty of this House of

The current value, according to a publication in the newspaper O Tempo, in this Tuesday, May 8, 2018 edition, will be the highest practiced among the five capitals where the Brazilian Urban Trains Company (CBTU) operates. And absurdly, the BH/Contagem Metro is only 28 km long. In Recife, for example, where the fare - even with the announced increase - will be lower than in Belo Horizonte, the metro has three lines and covers a total of 71 km, passing through 4 municipalities.

Comparing all the regions managed by CBTU, Belo Horizonte is the one that raises the most money in the country, however, the population does not see a return on what they pay. Absurdly, in addition to maintaining services from other states, since what is collected by the Belo Horizonte Metro goes to the company's single cash box, Minas Gerais is not treated as a priority when it comes to line expansion and improvements, a saga that has been dragging on for decades, marked by a game of "pass the buck", neglect and total apathy.

And to make matters worse, CBTU, once again, wants to shift the blame for poor management onto the "shoulders" of Minas Gerais users. The company shows no sensitivity, coherence, or efficiency. It seems unaware of the poor quality of services offered to the population, the bad working conditions imposed on metro employees, the current economic crisis in the country, the high number of unemployed, and the population's budget difficulties. The decision taken was disrespectful and, without a doubt, abusive and completely contrary to the current moment when the population demands transparency, efficient use of public resources collected, fair fares, and quality service.

In light of the above, it is necessary that the Ministry of Cities immediately suspend the 88.8% fare increase that will be charged to users of the BH/Contagem Metro and conduct a transparent and public process on the real need for fare composition and the investments that will be made in the population's benefit.

Chamber of Sessions, May 8, 2018.

WELITON PRADO

Consumer Defense Commission

**INDICATION No. 5.182, 2018**
(From Mr. Marco Tebaldi)
Requests from the Minister of Health urgent measures regarding the inclusion of Civil Police professionals in the preferential groups for receiving the H1N1 influenza virus vaccination.

**DISPOSITION:**
PUBLISH. FORWARD.

**To the Honorable Minister of Health:**

I am addressing Your Excellency to request, based on Article 113, I, of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies, urgent measures regarding the inclusion of Civil Police professionals in the preferential groups for receiving the H1N1 influenza virus vaccination.

Considering that the activities inherent to the performance of Civil Police functions place them in constant contact with people from diverse backgrounds, making them vulnerable to H1N1 influenza virus contamination, and that the absence of a professional from this institution due to non-vaccination, affecting a specific target group, will incur significant costs for society, which is already suffering from personnel shortages in the public security sector, and that the cost-benefit ratio strongly favors our proposal, we suggest to the Federal Government, through the bodies responsible for regulating the policies guiding the National Immunization Program, to conduct an in-depth study to include all Civil Police professionals in this preferential group.

INDICATION No. 5.183, 2018
(From Mr. Weliton Prado)
Suggests to the Ministry of Transportation, Ports and Civil Aviation, through the National Department of Transportation Infrastructure (DNIT), urgent measures to immediately begin operations of pothole filling and weed cutting along the BR-352, in the section between Coromandel and Abadia dos Durados, Alto Paranaíba.

DISPACH:
PUBLISH. FORWARD.

Excellent Lord,

Once again, the population is indignant with the precarious situation of the BR-352 between Coromandel and Abadia dos Dourados, Alto Paranaíba, which is under the responsibility of the National Department of Transportation Infrastructure (DNIT). This is because, while the federal government maintains neglect of this section, several accidents are being recorded and people are dying.

In just two days, major accidents marked the region. In two occurrences, six people were injured after the overturning of two vehicles attempting to avoid a pit in the road. The following day, a 15-year-old girl lost her life in another accident.

The outrage is so great that the population protested at the end of the week, as reported by the press and councilwoman-substitute Karina Oliveira. Thirty potholes were recorded on the highway, in addition to tall grass on the highway sides hindering drivers' visibility. The precariousness of the BR-352 still causes damage to cars and losses for small rural producers who need to use this section.

Therefore, it becomes urgent to prioritize and release resources for the immediate start of pothole filling and weed cutting works along the BR-352, in the section between Coromandel and Abadia dos Durados, breaking this process of neglect and apathy of the federal government towards Minas Gerais.

Chamber of Sessions, May 8, 2018.

INDICATION No. 5.184, 2018
(From Mr. Renzo Braz)
Suggests sending a sufficient number of textbooks to the municipality of Santa Bárbara do Leste, State of Minas Gerais, to meet the needs of all enrolled students.

DISPOSITION:
PUBLISH. FORWARD.

Most Honorable Minister of Education:

We address Your Excellency to present and claim the following:

- The number of books distributed by the National Textbook Program (PNLD) in the municipality of Santa Bárbara do Leste, State of Minas Gerais, was insufficient, particularly for the municipal schools of:

1. Manoel Martins de Oliveira;
2. Marlon dos Reis Lopes;
3. Francisco Inocêncio de Moura; and
4. Alvin Correa Faria Municipal Center for Child Education

These schools did not receive a sufficient number of textbooks to meet the needs of all enrolled students. There are classrooms where more than 40% of the students do not have a textbook, therefore lacking the minimum conditions for learning. Our children arrive at school and unfortunately do not have a minimum material for study. This is absurd! At the time of doing an exercise, each student wants to have their own book. Each one has their own pace and difficulties. Many cannot finish exercises in class and, to make matters worse, they cannot take the book home because the books need to be shared with students of the other shift. This puts the students' learning at risk.

There is a shortage of textbooks for all subjects to meet the needs of all enrolled students, in addition to a shortage of books for teachers.

- As per the FNDE website, "The FNDE distributes textbooks according to projections from the school census two years prior to the program year, which is the census available at the time of school selection processing."

- This distribution criterion, which generates a book shortage due to a technical deficiency in program management, has severe consequences for the students' learning in the region.

- The FNDE proposes to manage these fluctuations through redistribution, from schools with excess books to those with book shortages, or by using the technical reserve (a percentage of books made available to state education secretariats to accommodate new classes and enrollments).

INDICATION No. 5.185, 2018
(From Mr. Renzo Braz)
Recommends to the Minister of State that the necessary measures be adopted to regulate and make it viable
for the Federal Savings Bank to finance the entirety of the property related to housing, as well as reduce the
corresponding interest rates.
DISPOSITION:
PUBLISH. FORWARD.
Honorable Minister,
While we congratulate you on the efforts made so far in the framework of housing financing programs, we
emphasize the need for more effective measures to make it viable for the Federal Savings Bank (CEF) to
finance 100% of the property related to housing, as well as reduce the corresponding interest rates.
We thus aim to ensure that housing is a right accessible to all citizens, particularly the less favored
segment, who, in most cases, do not have any capital to provide as an "entry" or to cover residual values.
In fact, various media outlets repeatedly report that CEF has been applying financing interest rates above
those practiced by other financial institutions, including private ones.
It is important to highlight the report published on the UOL's economic website on March 27, 2018, with
the title: "Caixa loses leadership in housing financing for the fourth consecutive month."
According to the aforementioned article, until October 2017, CEF had always been the leader in housing
financing, far ahead of the second place in both the number of financed properties and values. In November,
it dropped to fourth place, behind Itaú Unibanco, Santander, and Bradesco, a situation that persisted in
December. In January 2018, Bradesco was first, followed by Santander, Caixa, and Itaú.
The fact is that, as published on the financial institution's own website, "since its creation in 1861, Caixa
has always sought to be more than just a bank, but a truly present institution in the lives of millions of
Brazilians. (...) It also appears at the moment of helping the population, through government social
programs, such as Bolsa Família - which benefits over 13 million Brazilians, FIES, and Minha Casa, Minha
Vida Program. (...) Throughout its history, Caixa has established close relations with the population by
meeting their immediate needs, such as savings, loans, FGTS, Social Integration Program (PIS),
Unemployment Insurance, educational credit, housing financing, and social benefit transfers."1

The current scenario therefore demonstrates the importance of keeping in mind the need for

**INDICATION No. 5.187, 2018**
**(From Mr. Weliton Prado)**
Suggests to the Minister of Agriculture, Livestock and Supply (MAPA), through the Minas Gerais Supply Centers S.A (Ceasa/MG), urgent measures to restore the trading hours of small producers and family farmers' products, currently held on Fridays at the Uberlândia unit in the Triangulo Mineiro region in the afternoon.

**DISPACH:**
**PUBLISH. FORWARD.**

Excellency,

Small producers and family farmers were surprised by another arbitrary and undiscussed decision by the Uberlândia Ceasa, which now aims to change the trading hours of products held at the unit on Fridays.

The trading has always been held in the afternoon to allow producers from Uberlândia and the entire region the necessary time to travel and organize their products. Indeed, most of them harvest their food in the morning to bring to Ceasa in the afternoon and offer fresh, new, and quality food/products to consumers over the weekend, as reinforced to our office by Zezinho Mendonça.

The change to morning hours should only occur after extensive discussion and consensus. The change drastically affects the lives of many people, the quality of products, not to mention the economic impact of the measure, which could lead to reduced purchases by the population and the safety of everyone with early morning displacements.

It is unbelievable that Ceasa, instead of focusing on solving problems at the unit, simply decides to change the trading hours of products without extensive discussion, without justification, and without consensus.

I am the author of the Chamber of Deputies Project of Law No. 59/2015, which establishes the National Plan for the Supply of Horticultural, Fruit, and Flower Products – PLANHORT – currently under review in the Senate after being approved by the Chamber of Deputies.

Therefore, we know and fight for the improvements and valorization of producers who trade at Ceasa. The suffering is immense and repeats every year.

According to UN data, family farming produces approximately 80% of the food consumed and preserves 75% of the planet's agricultural resources. In Brazil, family farmers are responsible for most of the food that reaches the population's table, ensuring food security, rural family permanence, and environmental preservation. There is no way to accept such disrespect, and the consequences of this measure will be negative for the budgets of families who depend on the Uberlândia Ceasa to trade their products; for consumers who may see product quality decrease; and for the economy of Uberlândia and the region.

Chamber Sessions Room, May 8, 2018.

WELITON PRADO
FEDERAL DEPUTY – PROS/MG

INDICATION No. 5.188, of 2018
(from Mr. Rômulo Gouveia)
Suggests sending an Indication to the Most Excellent Minister of National Integration, the resumption of
water supply by water truck in the rural areas of the Paraiban municipalities of Assunção, Barra de Santana,
Boqueirão, Campina Grande, Caturité, Coxixola, Fagundes, Gurjão, Lagoa Seca, Livramento, Queimadas, Parari,
Santa Luzia, Santo André, São José do Sabugi, São José dos Cordeiros, Serra Branca, and Taperoá.

MEMORANDUM:
FOR PUBLICATION. FOR FORWARDING.

TO: Honorable Minister of National Integration

Unfortunately, in my opinion, the Federal Government took a precipitate decision in
suspending the Water Truck Operation in 18 municipalities of Paraiba after cutting two-thirds of the resources
for water distribution, especially in rural areas, believing that significant rainfall had occurred in the cities.

However, not all municipalities have experienced significant reservoir replenishment, which could further
harm those living with water scarcity. There are regions that did not receive sufficient rainfall to even
increase reservoir levels by 10%. In these areas, the drought continues, and there is no water supply in the
city other than the water trucks.

Despite recent rainfall, municipalities continue to face difficulties in water distribution. The Federal
Government's measure was extreme. A survey should have been conducted beforehand to identify cities
with no rainfall and then reduce the amount, but cancelling it entirely at once became very complicated for
some cities, penalizing them.

Approximately 70,000 people, mostly from rural areas, who were being supplied through the water
trucks operation, are still facing difficulties in accessing potable water. Therefore, we request that the
operation be resumed immediately to avoid further disruptions to the beneficiaries.

Given the undeniable social impact of the issue, we count on your recognized sensitivity in approving
this Indication, with the resumption of water supply through water trucks in the rural areas of the
Paraiba municipalities of Assunção, Barra de Santana, Boqueirão, Campina Grande, Caturité, Coxixola,
Fagundes, Gurjão, Lagoa Seca, Livramento, Queimadas, Parari, Santa Luzia, Santo André, São José do
Sabugi, São José dos Cordeiros, Serra Branca, and Taperoá, which we suggest to Your Excellency as an
important and urgent measure.

Chamber of Sessions, May 9, 2018.

Rômulo Gouveia
Federal Deputy

**INDICATION No. 5.189, 2018**
(From Mr. Rômulo Gouveia)
Suggests to the Most Excellent Health Minister that the Mobile Component of Oral Health Care - Mobile Dental Unit (UOM) be implemented in the municipality of São Domingos do Cariri, state of Paraíba.

**DISPACH**
PUBLISH. FORWARD.

Most Excellent Health Minister:

The results of the latest oral health conditions survey of the Brazilian population (SB Brasil 2003) revealed an extremely alarming situation. According to data published on the Ministry of Health's website1, at that time, there were over 30 million edentulous people in the country, while almost the entire adult population had dental caries.

Since then, the topic has become an increasingly priority in the primary health care component offered by the Unified Health System (SUS). Among the various actions of the National Oral Health Policy, the Mobile Component of Oral Health Care, with the installation of Mobile Dental Units (UOM), is an extremely effective action for the care of our population. It specifically caters to those segments with difficulties in accessing health units.

The state of Paraíba has 223 municipalities, many of which have extensive rural areas. In this context, we consider that extending such assistance to all municipalities of the state will bring significant benefits to our population.

In light of the above, Mr. Minister, we suggest that the Mobile Component of Oral Health Care - Mobile Dental Unit (UOM) be installed in the municipality of São Domingos do Cariri/PB, which is fully justified under the proposed terms, as it is important and urgent.

Chamber of Sessions, May 9, 2018.

Deputado RÔMULO GOUVEIA
PSD-PB

Suggests to the Most Excellent Health Minister that the Mobile Component of Oral Health Care - Mobile Dental Unit (UOM) be implemented in the municipality of São José de Caiana, state of Paraíba.

DISPACH:
PUBLISH. FORWARD.

Most Excellent Health Minister:

The results of the latest oral health conditions survey of the Brazilian population (SB Brasil 2003) revealed an extremely alarming situation. According to data published on the Ministry of Health's website1, at that time, there were over 30 million edentulous people in the country, while almost the entire adult population had dental caries.

Since then, the issue has become an increasingly priority in the primary health care component offered by the Unified Health System (SUS). Among the various actions of the National Oral Health Policy, the Mobile Component of Oral Health Care, with the installation of Mobile Dental Units (UOM), is an extremely effective measure for the care of our population. It specifically addresses those segments with difficulties in accessing health units.

The state of Paraíba has 223 municipalities, many of which have extensive rural areas. In this context, we believe that extending such assistance to all municipalities of the state will bring significant benefits to our population.

In light of the above, Mr. Minister, we suggest that the Mobile Component of Oral Health Care - Mobile Dental Unit (UOM) be installed in the municipality of São José de Caiana/PB, which is fully justified under the proposed terms, as it is important and urgent.

DISPOSITION:
TO THE COMMISSION ON FINANCIAL INSPECTION AND CONTROL

EVALUATION:
Proposal Subject to Internal Review by the Commissions

Mr. President,

Based on Article 100, § 1, in conjunction with Articles 24, item X; 60, items I, II, and IV; and 61 of the Internal Regulation and Code of Conduct (RICD), and Articles 71, items IV, VI, VII, and VIII of the Federal Constitution, I propose that Your Excellency, after consulting the Plenum of this Commission, take the necessary measures to conduct, with the assistance of the Court of Accounts of the Union, an inspection and control act regarding possible financial irregularities committed by the National Council of Radiology Technicians and the Regional Council of Radiology Technicians of the 5th Region - São Paulo.

JUSTIFICATION
In view of the submission of a complaint accompanied by documents that reached my office through the President of the Union of Technologists, Technicians and Auxiliaries in Radiology of the State of São Paulo - SINTARESP, Mr. Sinclair Lopes de Oliveira, against the National Council of Radiology Technicians and the Regional Council of Radiology Technicians of the 5th Region - São Paulo, to which they present the following complaints of irregularities described below, this proposal is submitted.
May 2018

The current directors of CONTER and CRTR of the 5th Region, and CONTER, receive a bonus for attending meetings and commitments of the aforementioned archives, backed by CONTER resolution 12/2017, however, it came to the DENUNCIANT's knowledge that the accused DID NOT declare or pay income tax on the amounts received.

It should be clarified that the representation allowance and jetons paid to the counselors now accused, ARE IN FACT a "attendance bonus", the way counselors of CONTER and CRTRs, including CRTR/SP, are compensated for participating in meetings, plenaries, and other activities in the regions.

It is noted that this is not a cost of living allowance, a sum free of taxes, as the CONTER resolution does not establish that the board member present proof of expenses.

It is worth remembering that the IR regime follows the principle of universality, "which imposes equal treatment for all incomes, regardless of species or genre".

Thus, it is verified that the amounts received by the accused DO NOT have an indemnificatory nature, as there is no damage to be repaired to the board members' patrimony or conversion of a right they possess, but merely a remuneration for their work.

At this point, we have the regulation inserted in Article 153 of the CF/88:

Article 153. It is the Union's responsibility to establish taxes on:
III - income and profits of any kind;
§ 2º O the tax provided for in subparagraph III:
I - shall be determined by the criteria of generality, universality, and progressivity,
in accordance with the law.

"Article 2 - For the purposes of this Law, a public agent is anyone who exercises, even temporarily or without remuneration, by election, appointment, designation, contract, or any other form of investiture or link, a mandate, position, job, or function in the entities mentioned in the previous article."

It should be noted at this moment that Law No. 8.429/92 was more comprehensive than the Penal Code (art. 327) when defining the public agent, clearly stating in art. 1. that "any public agent, whether a servant or not, against the direct, indirect, or foundational administration of any of the powers of the Union, the states, the Federal District, the municipalities, a territory, a company incorporated into the public domain, or an entity for whose creation or funding the treasury has contributed or contributes with more than 50% (fifty percent) of the annual patrimony or revenue, shall be punished in accordance with this Law."

Article 2. complements the previous rule, stating that the Law applies to "anyone who exercises, even temporarily or without remuneration, by election, appointment, designation, contract, or any other form of investiture or bond, a mandate, position, employment, or function in the entities mentioned in the previous article."

(By Mr. Patrus Ananias and Mr. João Daniel)
Proposes that the Commission of Financial Inspection and Control, with the assistance of the Union Accounts Court (TCU), carry out an inspection and control act regarding the contract for the provision of business communication consulting services between Centrais Elétricas Brasileiras S.A. (Eletrobras) and RP Brasil Comunicações Ltda (FSB Comunicação).

**DISPACH**
**TO THE COMMISSION OF FINANCIAL INSPECTION AND CONTROL**

**CONSIDERATION**
Proposition subject to internal review within the Commissions

Mr. President,

Based on Article 100, § 1, in conjunction with Article 24, X, Article 60, II, and Article 61, § 1, of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies, and Articles 71, IV and VII of the Federal Constitution, and after consultation with the Plenary of this Commission, I propose, with the assistance of the Union Accounts Court (TCU), to carry out an inspection and control act regarding the contract for the provision of business communication consulting services between Centrais Elétricas Brasileiras S.A. (Eletrobras) and RP Brasil Comunicações Ltda (FSB Comunicação).

**JUSTIFICATION**

On April 24, 2018, the website Sportlight published that Centrais Elétricas Brasileiras S.A. (Eletrobras) contracted RP Brasil Comunicações Ltda to conduct a campaign against the very company it was contracted by. Given the seriousness of the allegation, the approval of the Proposal for Inspection and Control is of extreme importance to examine the validity of this contract. We reproduce the text published on Sportlight:

"Eletrobrás paid nearly R$ 2 million to worsen its own image"

Column notes, television comments, and agendas constructed to demonstrate the urgent need for privatization were driven by the FSB Comunicação group, through a "half-price" bidding process.

By Lúcio de Castro, Sportlight, published April 24, 2018 - 14h25

Wilson Ferreira Júnior assumed the Eletrobrás with a specific mission given by Michel Temer: to conduct the privatization process.

Officially referred to as "deregulation" or "democratization of capital," the privatization of the company, a priority of the Michel Temer government, received a significant boost on September 20, 2017, when the state signed a contract with RP Brasil Comunicações, part of the FSB Comunicação group, the country's largest press office.

**CONTRACT OBJECT**

The contract ECE-DJS 1252/2017, obtained by the reporting team through the Access to Information Law (LAI): "to advise Eletrobras on communication related to the majority shareholder's privatization project for the company."

In search of public mobilization and a favorable environment for privatization, the company adopted as a strategy the dissemination of a scenario of miseries and problems of the state-owned company. To do this, it was necessary to engage so-called opinion formers, the press, release notes in newspaper columns, arm economic commentators, and set the media agenda, always presenting a scenario that made such privatization urgent, accelerated by the federal government's haste to finalize the deal. The company denies such bias and states that the contract emphasizes the need to "preserve the company's positive image," although it admits that the disclosure "does not omit negative data such as financial losses or gross debt exceeding R$ 45 billion" (see "the other side at the end of the report").

According to the plan outlined in the contract, a "scenario analysis" was conducted, followed by the so-called "mapping of stakeholders," that is, defining who is the strategic target audience for the messages to be sent. In a second moment, came the "mobilization of influencers," an item detailed with a cost of R$ 170,000.00 (one hundred and seventy thousand) within the total project cost of R$ 800,000.00.

One of the 10 items included in the FSB action plan and presented in the contract was the conduct of an opinion poll to verify the popularity of the plan to privatize Eletrobras, with a specific cost of R$ 120,000.00 (one hundred and twenty thousand).

The contract between Eletrobras and FSB also stipulates in item 7.1 that payments between the contracting entity and the contracted party will be made upon the "delivery of the monthly reports prepared by the contracted party corresponding to the consolidation of the achieved results." The report requested these reports through another access to information request law, but although the contract itself was made available through the access to information law, even in a final instance, access to the reports was denied.

A third access to information request was made to Eletrobras regarding information about the alleged bidding process for the relevant contract, ECE-DJS 1252/2017. The request sought the names of the bidders, the proposals, the process documents, and the final result. It was also denied at both the first and second instance.

In the denial, Eletrobras justifies the secrecy regarding the bidding process as part of what it calls "social capital democratization," stating that "it concerns a strategic information of Eletrobras, since the requested documents are directly linked to the company's activities in the competitive market." It continues: "This is because the information regarding the contract with RP Brasil Comunicações (FSB Comunicação) is a fundamental pillar of Eletrobras' social capital democratization process." It also highlights the strategic importance of the contract between Eletrobras and FSB: "Indeed, it is worth noting that the disclosure of information regarding the Contract with RP can be so sensitive that it may cause harm to the so-called democratization process."

The report filed an appeal with the General Control of the Union (CGU), arguing the contradiction between having access to the contract but being denied access to the reports and bidding process, as well as other access to information law issues that guarantee such access. The CGU has not responded yet.

Despite Eletrobras' denial of transparency in the access to the bidding process, the report investigated, through various sources, how the competition unfolded. Or, more accurately, how it did not unfold. At least from a certain point.

In the midst of the Temer government's rush to privatize Eletrobras, a "price taking" was conducted to determine who would win the ECE-DJS 1252/2017 contract. Price taking is a crucial moment in a bidding process where the price threshold for the final auction is determined, and market price parameters are demonstrated. It is also, in a general and generic sense, a moment in the bidding process where prices can be inflated and overcharged.

The book "An Analysis in the Light of the Vulnerabilities of Public Tenders in Brazil" (José Luciano de Oliveira, Descartes Almeida Fontes, Rodrigo Alexandre, and Bruno Andrey) shows that, again in a general sense, "in this phase, various types of fraud can occur, such as bid rigging, pre-agreement, price fixing, overcharging, and the qualification of non-existent companies."

Typically, three budgets from different companies are used. When contracting the services in question, the institution conducts the tender procedures in accordance with specific legislation, and both companies that were budgeted in the price taking phase and any other company can participate, as long as they observe market values. Thus, whenever the price taking stage is won, a tender is held.

The unusual is what happened at Eletrobras regarding the ECE-DJS 1252/2017 contract, according to various sources interviewed by Sportlight Investigative Journalism Agency. The reports, which complement each other, state that some of the country's largest companies in the advisory and communication sector participated in the competition. In addition to FSB, proposals were submitted by Companhia de Noticias (CDN) and Informe Comunicação. The three occupy the podium

May 2018

in government accounts with recognized expertise in communication strategy.
According to the investigation by the report, Informe Comunicação presented the proposal with the lowest financial cost, ranking first. FSB came in second. However, after the result of the "price quote" from companies called for a bidding process, the rules changed: Eletrobras decided to choose the winner through the "inexibility" modality, where competition is dispensed and direct contracting is promoted. The law grants the right to the contractor to choose the supplier if there are reasons to justify the dispensation of bidding.
In the relevant contract, Eletrobras argued that "due to its complexity and singularity, as well as confidentiality, involving strategic information of the company, it could only be done through the inapplicability of bidding, which makes it impossible to establish objective criteria, requiring a company with recognized expertise in communication strategy" as stated in Eletrobras' response at the end of the report in "Another Perspective". The other parties involved in the "price quote" have contracts with other entities of the same federal government to develop communication strategies.
On October 17, 2017, almost a month after the signing of the contract between FSB and Eletrobras, the company published the result in the Official Gazette of the Union, announcing the result with FSB as the holder of the contract by "inexibility of bidding".

The behind-the-scenes of the non-competition point to a decisive hand in choosing
after the price taking by "unavailability of bidding" that declared the victory of FSB:
Wilson Pinto Ferreira Junior, appointed by Michel Temer to preside the state-owned company.

In 1998, he moved to the private sector as the first president of Rio Grande Energia, created after the partial privatization of electricity distribution in the state of Rio Grande do Sul by then-governor Antônio Britto. He took over the presidency of the CPFL company in March 2000 and has been presiding the holding since 2002.
The appointment of Wilson Pinto Ferreira Júnior by Michel Temer was on July 22, 2016.

The rapporteur of the MP for privatizing Eletrobras is listed in the Odebrecht bribe list by the nicknames "Pavão", "Bonitão", "Bonitinho", "Velho", and "Casa de Doido". Former Deputy Pedro Corrêa cites the rapporteur of MP 814/2017 in his testimony as follows: "This guy needs to be investigated. He made a mess at the Rio de Janeiro secretariat." Júlio Lopes denies all accusations.
In its propaganda, the government boasts that it will achieve R$ 12.2 billion through privatization, always referred to as "democratization of capital." However, according to the Ministry of Mines and Energy itself, the state-owned company's patrimonial value is R$ 46.2 billion, and the company's total assets reach R$ 170.5 billion. In addition to R$ 541 billion invested since its creation in 1962.
A war of injunctions and in the National Congress has been waged on this topic. To try to win the information battle, Eletrobras launched a communication campaign for the "majority shareholder's project for the company's privatization," which is included in the contract discussed here, the ECE-DJS 1252/2017, from the bidding that ended with FSB. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION No. 3,494, 2018
(from Ms. Cristiane Brasil)
Requests information from the Minister of State for Transportation, Ports and Civil Aviation on the measures taken
after the collapse that occurred in the works of the highway BR-040 in Petrópolis/RJ in November 2017.
DISPACH:
Approval by the President, Dep. Rodrigo Maia, "ad referendum" of the Desk, of the opinion of Mr. Dep. Fábio Ramalho, First Vice-President, for forwarding.

Mr. President:
I request from Your Excellency, based on Article 50 of the Federal Constitution and in accordance with Articles 115 and 116 of the Internal Regulation, that, after consulting the Desk, information be requested from Mr. State Minister of Transport, Ports and Civil Aviation, in order to clarify this House regarding the problems that occurred on the margins of the highway BR-040 in Petrópolis/RJ, especially regarding actions aimed at ensuring the life, security and housing of the citizens affected by the disaster that occurred in November 2017.

JUSTIFICATION

A landslide caused the formation of a crater on the side of the BR-040 highway, at kilometer 81, heading towards Rio de Janeiro, on November 7, 2017. This event immediately destroyed dozens of homes, others had to be demolished later due to irreparable damage, and over fifty were closed, leaving over a hundred people homeless in the region known as Vale da Escola. A municipal school was also affected, preventing over seventy students from attending classes.

The affected people, even after more than five months, still lack adequate assistance and demand a definitive solution. Despite the initiatives of the Civil Defense of Petrópolis Municipality, the Federal Public Ministry, and the orders of the 4th Civil Court of Petrópolis, the highway concessionaire, Concer, remains inactive regarding the matter and has contributed little to solving the problem.

An inspection report prepared by IBAMA identified that the cause of the incident is related to problems in the construction of a tunnel. According to the report, signs that the structure could collapse were already noticeable long before the event, and the lack of rainfall in the state of Rio de Janeiro was what prevented the collapse from happening earlier.

However, the fact that the work had been halted since the previous year contributed both to the
inability to identify the problem in a timely manner and to the degradation of the already completed parts of the work.
According to the report, continuing the work would prevent water accumulation, which is a determining factor for the collapse.
Even more concerning is the fact that the problem may recur in the same
location if the drainage and containment works recommended in the Technical Report of the Civil Defense Secretariat and Voluntary Actions of the Municipality of Petrópolis are not carried out. Regarding these works, the Federal Public Ministry requested a conciliation hearing in February 2018, aiming to have Concer carry out these actions.
The construction of a new climb up the Petrópolis mountain range was considered the most important
improvement to the BR-040 highway by the Highway Exploration Program, as per the concession contract signed in 1995. However, the start of the works, initially planned for the first year of the concession in 2011, was only effectively executed in 2013 and 2014.
In addition, the implementation cost, estimated at R$ 80 million in April 1995, which
today would correspond, in updated values, to approximately R$ 330 million, jumped to R$ 897 million
after the concessionaire submitted the basic project in 2012, a threefold increase.
In 2015, the National Development Bank - BNDES - approved a loan of R$ 420 million for investments in the aforementioned work.
However, the Federal Public Ministry points out irregularities, on the part of the National Land Transport Agency - ANTT, in the approval of the start of the works regarding requirements provided for in Law No. 8.666/93, the so-called Law of Tenders, and in the release of resources through a contract addendum in violation of the Annual Budget Law of 2014 and the 1988 Federal Constitution.
The Union Accounts Court - TCU - identified, through processo nº 023.204/2015-0 in 2016,
irregularities in the implementation of the concession contract, such as overvaluation of the amount
necessary for economic and financial rebalancing, overpricing in the work budget, and outdated and deficient basic and executive projects.
Administrators of the Triunfo Group - controller of Concer - were recently denounced
by the Public Ministry in Operation Integration, the 48th phase of Lava Jato, which investigates diversions and
frauds in tenders at the Department of Roads and Highways of Paraná.
Thus, the scenario is extremely concerning and the situation of the affected families demands
urgent and definitive solutions. It is not acceptable that citizens have their right to housing restricted due
to successive failures of the Public Administration and the concessionaires to whom public services are granted. In this particular case, we refer to the citizens affected by the incident that occurred on the margins of the BR-040 in Petrópolis, almost six months ago.

3) What has the Concessionaire and ANTT been doing to prevent similar tragedies from occurring again in the BR-040 project in Petrópolis?

Mr. President,

I request, based on Article 50, § 2 of the Federal Constitution, in conjunction with Article 115, I, and 116 of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies, that, after consulting the Desk, a request for information be sent to His Excellency, Minister of State for Foreign Affairs, Aloysio Nunes Ferreira, regarding the situation of the Brazilian Evangelical Community in Rwanda, especially of the missionaries, following the recent closure of hundreds of Evangelical churches and the arrest of Protestant pastors by the government of that country.

JUSTIFICATION

In recent days, the media has reported that the Rwandan government has closed hundreds of churches and dozens of mosques. The government has banned over 6,000 churches and around 100 mosques. The majority of the closed churches are Pentecostal.

The government claims that the closed churches and mosques failed to meet safety and noise pollution standards set by Rwandan law. The move followed a catastrophe at a church where 16 worshippers died and 140 were injured after lightning struck the building. According to the government spokesperson, churches and mosques can resume their activities if they meet the standards established by law.

According to the press, the closures are actually aimed at exerting greater control over the growing religious community in the African country3. According to Rwandan President Paul Kagame, the number of religious groups in the country has increased significantly in recent years.

The Washington Post. Rwanda closes thousands of churches in bid for more control. <https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/africa/rwanda-closes-thousands-of-churches-in-bid-for-more- control/2018/04/04/1a758880-37f0-11e8-af3c-2123715f78df_story.html?utm_term=.e238679537a9>
May 2018
DIARY OF THE HOUSE OF DEPUTIES
Tuesday 15 193

The number of churches and mosques is excessive for a country as small as Rwanda. According to BBC4, six pastors who defied the state order were arrested by the Rwandan police, accused of promoting subversive gatherings.

Human Rights Defenders argue that the closure of churches and mosques follows a government campaign against freedom of expression. A proposal to regulate religious organizations separately from other civil society organizations is pending in the Rwandan Parliament. The proposal is expected to be approved by the Legislative Power, given the government's support from the majority of parliamentarians.

It is in these terms that we request the above information, so that we may know the situation of the Brazilian Evangelical community in Rwanda, particularly the missionaries.

Meeting Room, April 18, 2018.

Based on Article 50, §2 of the Federal Constitution and in accordance with Articles 115 and 116 of the Internal Regulation of the Chamber of Deputies, I request that the Honorable Minister of State for Finance be provided with information regarding the actions of the Central Bank in recent years through committed operations and currency swaps.

The actions of the Central Bank in recent years involved a significant volume of resources (hundreds of billions of reais) in operations known in the market as "Committed Operations" and "Currency Swaps", which need to be better explained not only regarding their role in monetary policy, but also as to their impacts on economic policy as a whole.

In light of the above, I request the following questions be answered.

Respectfully,

Session Room,

Federal Deputy

**Inquiries:**
**Regarding Committed Operations and Their Impact on Public Debt**

1) Why has the volume of committed operations grown so much (from 3.2% of the total Gross Government Debt in November 2002 to 24.7% in August 2017)?
2) Why, instead of significantly increasing the balance of committed operations, were these operations not combined with the definitive sale of public titles held by the Central Bank, thereby reducing its stock and contributing to the National Treasury's efforts to lengthen the profile of public debt?
3) Why does the Central Bank hold in its portfolio an amount of public titles exceeding 20% of GDP, while the international average is below 5%?
4) What is the need for the Central Bank to maintain a portfolio with such a high volume of public titles, given that Law No. 11,803 of 2008 provides for the possibility of transferring public titles from the National Treasury to the Central Bank whenever necessary to cover the latter's negative results or to meet monetary policy needs, with prior authorization from the Minister of Finance and without financial counterparty?
5) It is observed that much of the effort conducted by the National Treasury to lengthen the average maturities of public debt and reduce the percentage of papers corrected by the Selic rate has been "annulled" by the increase in the stock of committed operations, which are characterized by extremely short terms and interest rates, although fixed, that express the current Selic rate. How is coordination between the actions of the National Treasury and the Central Bank aimed at improving the profile of public debt?
6) By maintaining a stock of committed operations exceeding R$ 1 trillion, which needs to be constantly renewed, how vulnerable does the Central Bank (and consequently the Brazilian economy) become to a speculative attack by the financial market? Justify.
7) In what way does the separate management of the two essential components (on one side, public titles managed by the National Treasury; on the other, committed operations administered by the Central Bank) compromise the effectiveness of public debt management?
8) Why do committed operations not appear in the Annual Financing Plans (PAFs), an instrument for planning the management of public titles prepared by the National Treasury Secretariat, since they fall within both the scope of Liquid Public Debt (DLSP) and Gross General Government Debt (DBGG)?
9) What should be the limit for the amount of federal mobile debt referred to in Article 48, paragraph XIV of the Constitution?
a. Should this limit be established for gross debt, liquid debt, or both? Justify.

10) Should there be a limit to the volume of the portfolio of public debt securities held by the Central Bank? Justify.
a. If so, what should be this limit? Justify.
b. If the current volume exceeds the limit proposed in the previous question, what strategy has been adopted to reduce it?
11) Should the Central Bank be authorized to accept and pay interest on voluntary deposits at sight or term from financial institutions? Justify.
c. If so, would voluntary deposits contribute to maintaining the high spreads already charged by financial institutions, as they would have an additional incentive to invest their resources in public securities instead of expanding credit supply? Justify.

**JUSTIFICATION**

This federal deputy's two Information Requests from the Chamber of Deputies regarding the subject matter at hand—Brazilian citizens' access to classified information concerning the registration and study of unidentified flying objects (UFOs) and their crew, commonly known as ufology—are referenced as:

RIC 
4470/2009 
679/2011

These were partially answered by the three Armed Forces, representing primarily the Ministry of Defense, within what the Forces claim to be the truth reported in their subordinate bodies' archives. These responses confirmed not only the existence of such information but also some incidents involving alleged UFOs and their crew, as well as the seriousness with which at least the Brazilian Air Force (FAB) handles the matter. Today, there are over 10,000 pages of documents and other types of information in various formats, collected in batches and held by the National Archive in Brasília and Rio de Janeiro, all sent by FAB. This does not include the procedures of this Force regarding the collection, registration, archiving, and subsequent retrieval of materials to public archives, outlined in Portaria 551/GC3 of August 9, 2010, published by FAB and known among scholars and specific media as the "ET Law."

Despite the efforts demonstrated by the Brazilian Air Force, many issues raised in previous requests remain unresolved. Over time—it has been seven years since the last RIC's responses—there is no similar willingness from the other forces, the Army and Navy, to provide data to interested citizens, as the same phenomenon that led FAB to adopt and publish its procedures for registration and archiving occurs not only in air space but also over and under Brazilian territorial waters, and its activity is also recorded on land, across the 8.5 million square kilometers of Brazilian territory, making it a matter to be addressed not by one but by all three defense forces of the national territory.

In particular, the justificatory basis for this Request focuses on seeking information about a specific case of significant national impact and worldwide resonance, known in the media as "The Varginha ET Case" or among ufologists as "The Varginha Case," as it occurred in that Minas Gerais city in early 1996 and its press coverage lasted at least another year. This case is of singular importance for several reasons, but two are of paramount importance to scientific knowledge and the transparency of public acts: first, because, according to ufologists, it involves the crash of an unknown-technology UFO and the capture of at least two of its crew, and second, due to the impressive cover-up operation of the facts, for reasons that are not yet fully clear. Suspicions also lead to another serious conclusion, regarding a possible breach of national sovereignty, as the final destination of the crashed ship's materials and captured bodies, according to ufologists, was the United States of America, against the wishes of several officers, for obvious reasons.

The lack of public information about the case, considered true by a large portion of Varginha's population, results in prejudice, ridicule, embarrassment, pain, and doubt among witnesses and relatives of those directly involved, such as the family of military police officer Marco Eli Chereze, who was reportedly a fatal victim of direct contact with one of the crew members.

Under the LAI (Law of Access to Information), which was sanctioned after the aforementioned __UFO_PROTECTED_000__s were answered, new questions about the procedures, especially those of the Army, were raised. Since 2012, several requests have been made to the Federal Government's Electronic Service of Citizen Information (e-SIC), all denied or answered in a way that does not reveal what may remain classified. This is the case, for example, with the strange absence, to date, on the Army's website, of the Document Indexing Codes (CIDICs) containing classified information, originating in 1996 and 1997. According to Article 45, Item II of Decree No. 7,724, one of the decrees that emerged to complement and give effect to the LAI, all documents still classified should have their identifications in code format available on a specific list, on the electronic pages of the public bodies responsible for them, by June 1st of each year. If these documents do indeed exist and were generated between 1996 and 1997, as we are shown by...

an abundance of circumstantial and testimonial evidence; to remain classified, they could only have been
designated as ULTRASECRET at the time, with a 25-year secrecy period. Indeed, one of the main military witnesses
in the Varginha Case categorically stated in a recorded deposition that the operation to transport the unknown
biological entities, crew members of the crashed UFO, from the ESA to Campinas (Unicamp)
on January 23, 1996, was treated as ULTRASECRET by commanders and thus classified in that category. Therefore,
their records could only be made publicly available on January 24, 2021, although the CIDIC identifying the
event should already exist and be available to interested parties. Yet, if Decree 7.724 entered into force on May
16, 2012, why has the Army not yet made available in its "list of ultra-secret information" the CIDICs for this and
other Varginha Case occurrences, six years after the LAI's implementation?

In addition to this issue, it is noticed that at the location designated for publishing the "list of classified and
declassified information from the Army," whose address is http://www.eb.mil.br/informacoes-classificadas-, there are no suggestions from
the "Guide for Publishing the List of Classified and Declassified Information and Statistical Reports on the
Access to Information Law," available on the e-SIC of the Ministry of Transparency and Control General of the
Union (CGU), accessible at: http://www.acessoainformacao.gov.br/lai-para-sic/sic-apoio-orientacoes/guias-e-orientacoes/guia- informacoes-classificadas-versao-3.pdf. In this CGU-drafted guide, under
subitem B.2.4 - Content of the "classified information list" - it clearly states: "it is also
recommended that the agency or entity disclose the subject matter of the classified document, with the aim of
increasing transparency regarding its content, as well as allowing social control. It is emphasized that
including the subject in the list of classified documents aids in future reference identification, as provided in
Article 30, II, Law No. 12.527/2011. To do so, the agency should inform as broadly as possible
the content of the document, without, however, revealing the restricted information. This recommendation is
simply ignored by the Army.

It is also noteworthy in this list of classified documents, designated as ULTRASECRET, that only those whose
secrecy periods expire or in the previous year, or in the year of the list's publication, up to June 1st, are
made public. Thus, until June 1st, 2017 - the last update was made in 2016 - all ULTRASECRET documents were
about to lose their secrecy period, i.e., those with their origin registered up to 1992, 25 years prior. There is
none in this timeframe that was classified as ULTRASECRET after 1992. It is also noticed that all those
classified in this category already have approved reclassification suggestions, i.e., with an additional 25 years
of secrecy. There is no record of a document classified at the highest level of secrecy that has not been
reclassified, or even declassified, after the LAI's implementation. If this logic persists, which overrides the
exception to maintain secrecy in favor of the LAI's transparency recommendation, the first documents on the
Varginha Case will only have their CIDICs made public at the expiration of their secrecy period in 2021, and
already reclassified in the same category, remaining hidden from society until 2046.

Once again, calling for public bodies to adhere to the Constitutional Principle of Publicity of Official Acts,
Article 37 of the CF, especially noting that the maintenance of secrecy regarding the facts revealed here, this
request has significant public and scientific interest.
Brasília, May 2, 2018.
